Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production transparent photographic sprite atlas for the game I Was Away.
Reference image 1 is the existing eight-angle standing turnaround and defines the exact identity, clothing, camera, backpack and direction. Reference image 2 is the existing front-right animation and defines realistic cutout photography and pose vocabulary. Do not copy the bad invisible RGB artifacts.
Create a NEW directional animation atlas of this exact man viewed STRAIGHT FROM THE FRONT, facing the viewer with chest and both shoulders visible symmetrically, in every cell. Preserve dark brown skin, short thick dreadlocks, close beard, charcoal-brown T-shirt with small worn offwhite I Was Away lettering and boomerang motif, blue jeans, grey-brown trail shoes, charcoal camera backpack with its attached collapsed tripod, black DSLR camera ALWAYS present, wristwatch on the man's left wrist. Same adult identity and proportions. Do not mirror existing art.
Exactly 16 separated full-body sprites in a strict 4-column by 4-row equal-cell grid, reading left to right. Each cell has generous transparent margin; no character crossing a cell boundary. Uniform camera distance, identical body scale, fixed ground baseline near the bottom of each equal cell. Natural photo detail, realistic soft neutral light. Actual transparent alpha background, NO floor, NO shadows cast outside the person, NO checker pattern, NO labels, NO border or numbering.
Row 1: (0) relaxed standing camera lowered in right hand; (1) standing camera held in both hands at chest height; (2) standing lifting the camera halfway toward face; (3) standing shooting with camera at right eye aimed straight toward viewer.
Row 2: (4) walking first stride right foot forward camera safely in right hand; (5) walking passing feet; (6) walking opposite stride left foot forward camera in right hand; (7) walking second passing feet. Real alternating-leg movement.
Row 3: (8) bent knees half-crouching while camera stays at eye; (9) full low squat photographing; (10) slightly adjusted full low squat photographing; (11) standing photographing with elbows slightly tucked, a second shooting keyframe.
Row 4: (12) half-kneeling down with camera at eye; (13) right knee on ground, left foot planted, photographing; (14) same knee-down position with slightly adjusted camera aim; (15) relaxed standing camera at chest height after photographing.
Important: crouching and kneeling figures must be genuinely lower within their fixed cells, NOT enlarged to fill the cell. The ground under shoes stays aligned. Every view is directly front-facing, not three-quarter. All 16 complete bodies and all hands/cameras fully inside their own cell.
